domain: Responsible AI Governance & Global Regulatory Compliance
title: Navigating EU AI Act Compliance Mandates for High-Risk Automated Hiring Algorithms
context: You are VP of AI at an enterprise HR tech company. The EU AI Act takes full effect, classifying your candidate screening and scoring engine as a 'High-Risk AI System'. Regulators demand strict audit trails, bias mitigation, and human oversight guarantees under penalty of heavy fines.
dilemma: How do you restructure the enterprise AI governance committee, algorithm audit process, and engineering pipelines without freezing current product revenue streams?

key_competencies: Regulatory Compliance (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF)
must_include: Establishing a cross-functional AI Ethics & Compliance Board
Third-party algorithmic bias auditing (Disparate Impact ratio)
common_pitfalls: Shutting down products completely out of fear

star_model_answer.situation: The EU AI Act designated our core candidate screening AI system as High-Risk, requiring immediate compliance transformation.
star_model_answer.task: As VP of AI, establish compliant AI governance and technical validation to maintain EU market access.
star_model_answer.action: I instituted an AI Ethics & Governance Board with Legal, Engineering, and Product leads. I mandated independent third-party bias audits, refactored our model training pipeline to enforce equalized odds metric thresholds, and implemented a mandatory Human-in-the-Loop verification gate for all candidate rejection recommendations.
star_model_answer.result: Achieved full EU AI Act conformity certification 3 months ahead of deadline, preserving $18M in European annual recurring revenue.

domain: AI Talent Scaling, Organization Design & Budget Allocation
title: Structuring an Enterprise AI Organization: Centralized AI Center of Excellence vs Embedded Squads
context: An enterprise with 5,000 employees has scattered AI shadow projects across marketing, engineering, and finance. High turnover in AI talent is caused by lack of career ladders, and infrastructure costs are spiraling due to duplicate GPU cloud instances.
dilemma: How do you design a hybrid Hub-and-Spoke AI organizational model, establish shared infrastructure guardrails, and retain elite AI talent?

must_include: AI career ladders (Research Scientist vs MLOps Engineer vs Product AI)
common_pitfalls: Over-centralizing AI and creating an ivory tower disconnected from business units

star_model_answer.situation: Disorganized shadow AI initiatives across business units caused $2M in redundant GPU expenses and high AI engineer turnover.
star_model_answer.task: Re-architect the enterprise AI organization for scale, operational governance, and talent retention.
star_model_answer.action: I designed and executed a Hub-and-Spoke AI organizational model. The Hub (AI CoE) manages core infrastructure, MLOps tooling, security guardrails, and career frameworks, while Spoke AI engineers are embedded directly into business unit product squads to drive localized domain impact.
star_model_answer.result: Infrastructure costs decreased by 35% through shared resource pool management, AI talent retention increased by 85%, and feature deployment velocity doubled.
